## Ephemerides (`ephem/<body>.csv`, hourly)

Bodies: 3i_atlas (Horizons `C/2025 N1`, solution JPL#54), earth 399, stereo_a -234, solar_orbiter -144, parker_solar_probe -96, bepicolombo -121, mars 499, maven -202, venus 299, mercury 199, juice -28, psyche -255, europa_clipper -159. ace -92 and wind -8 are included as extras.

Source: JPL Horizons API, `EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS`, `CENTER=500@10`, `REF_PLANE=FRAME` (ICRF), `VEC_CORR=NONE` (geometric, no light time), `TIME_TYPE=UT`, 1 h step. The raw text is in `raw/horizons/*_icrf.txt`.

Columns:
- `utc`: UTC time of the record.
- `x_hci_km, y_hci_km, z_hci_km` and `vx_hci, vy_hci, vz_hci` (km/s): Heliocentric Inertial, as in the sunpy `HeliocentricInertial` frame (Thompson 2006). Z is the IAU solar pole (RA 286.13 deg, Dec 63.87 deg). X is the ascending node of the solar equator on the mean J2000 ecliptic. HCRS to HCI is a constant rotation, taken from sunpy 8.0.1.
- `r_au`: heliocentric distance in AU (1 AU = 149597870.7 km).
- `hgi_lon_deg, hgi_lat_deg`: spherical HCI coordinates.
- `carr_lon_deg, carr_lat_deg`: sunpy `HeliographicCarrington` with `observer="earth"`. This applies the conventional Earth-observer light-time definition of the Carrington meridian, so all bodies share one rotating frame at each time. Using `observer="self"` instead would shift the comet by about 0.07 deg.
- `heeq_lon_deg, heeq_lat_deg`: sunpy `HeliographicStonyhurst`, with longitude wrapped to (-180, 180].
- `ecl_lon_deg, ecl_lat_deg`: heliocentric ecliptic J2000. This is the ICRF vector rotated by the IAU76 obliquity of 84381.448 arcsec, the convention of Horizons `refplane=ecliptic` that the preprint used.

Checks (`ephem/frame_checks.json`):
- HCI latitude agrees with Horizons `REF_PLANE=BODY` (IAU_SUN body equator) to 1e-14 deg at 9 epochs for the comet, Earth, STEREO-A and PSP. The longitude offset is a constant -61.1005 deg (peak-to-peak 1e-13 deg); it is the arc between the two nodes that define each frame's x-axis.

## Cross-check against the preprint caches (`qc/crosscheck_preprint.json`, `qc/crosscheck_preprint.png`)

The preprint caches cover 2025-11-08 to 2025-12-29; the overlap with this work is 2025-11-08 to 2025-12-19. Before comparing, the cache values are given the preprint's own validity filter (0.01<n<500, 100<v<1500, PLS1800 = 52).
- Same products:
  - SolO COHO, ACE K1 and OMNI2 are identical to the caches (max |Δ| = 0).
  - STA COHO differs by at most 0.05 cm^-3 and 0.5 km/s, a rounding-level difference that suggests a reprocessing since the cache was made.
- Hourly means rebuilt from high-resolution data:
  - Binned on [tag, tag+1 h), STA PLASTIC 1-min reproduces STA COHO with median ratio 1.000, |Δn| <= 0.005, |Δv| <= 0.05.
  - SolO PAS reproduces SolO COHO with median ratio 1.000; the 5–95% ratio range is within ±0.8% in n and +0.3% in v.
  - Binning on [tag-30 min, tag+30 min) is clearly worse: only 65% of STA hours agree within 10%. This confirms that COHO tags mark the start of the hour, as the CDF states.
- OMNI: hourly means of OMNI_HRO2 against the cached OMNI2 give median ratio 1.000 and r(log n) = 0.988.
- Wind: unshifted Wind H1 matches cached OMNI2 best at a +1 h lag (median n ratio 1.004, r(log n) = 0.995). This lag is the propagation shift from Wind to the bow-shock nose.
- ACE K1 against Wind H1 for the same hour: v ratio 0.996, but the median n ratio is 0.66, with 5–95% range 0.23–0.96. The preprint scaled ACE n by a fixed factor of 1.7, which corresponds to a ratio of 0.59.
- Preprint timing: the preprint used COHO start-of-hour tags as sample times, while its OMNI2 tags are hour centers. This mixes conventions with a 30-min offset; the effect is small compared with the mapping uncertainty.

## Caveats and decisions

- No contemporaneous heavy-ion composition exists on CDAWeb for October–December 2025:
  - ACE SWICS (AC_H3_SW2) ends 2025-03-16. The ACE Science Center SWICS 2.0 file for 2025 also stops at DOY 76.
  - AC_H6_SWI ends 2024-12-31.
  - Solar Orbiter SWA-HIS L3 (SOLO_L3_SWA-HIS-COMP-10MIN) ends 2023-04-27, and ESA SOAR also has no HIS science products after 2023-04-28.
  - STA PLASTIC Fe charge states end in 2011.
  - The only composition columns are therefore alpha/proton ratios (OMNI NaNp_Ratio, Wind Na/Np, ACE K1 He_ratio).
- ACE SWEPAM:
  - Level 2 (AC_H0_SWE) ends 2024-07-09, both on CDAWeb and at the ASC, so only the preliminary K1 browse data exist for this period.
  - K1 densities run low against Wind (median ratio 0.66) and show deep dropouts around Nov 14–20. Use ACE for speed and structure, not for absolute n.
- OMNI: for the whole period both OMNI_HRO2 IMF and PLS are 100% Wind (ID 52), and OMNI2 uses IDs 51/52. OMNI therefore adds no independent spacecraft; it is Wind time-shifted to the bow-shock nose.
- DSCOVR: DSCOVR_H1_FC on CDAWeb ends 2019-06-27, and the NCEI DSCOVR archive has moved behind a portal, so DSCOVR was not used.
- Wind: WI_K0_SWE was also fetched (`raw/hapi/WI_K0_SWE`) but rejected, because QF_V and QF_Np are never 0 in this period and their semantics could not be confirmed. Wind H1 has many gaps; OMNI is the more complete L1 series.
- STEREO-A PLASTIC:
  - The 2025 L2 files carry no RTN velocity, no E/W flow angle (fill) and no `caution` flag. Requesting any of those parameters makes HAPI return "no data", so they were dropped.
  - The `error` and `attitude_flag` columns are empty but kept.
  - COHO flow angles are fill.
- Solar Orbiter PAS:
  - `quality_factor` has no definition in the CDF metadata or the PAS user guide. It is kept as a column and not used for filtering; COHO does not filter on it either.
  - Hours where V_RTN is missing but N exists (for example 2025-12-05T15 to 12-06T13, with T near 5e5 K) are rejected entirely, which matches COHO.
- Parker Solar Probe:
  - SPC L3I returns no data from October to December 2025.
  - SPAN-I partial moments outside encounter (SUN_DIST 0.4–0.73 AU, before 2025-12-06) give n of about 0.1–2 cm^-3, roughly 10x below expectation, because of the field-of-view and heat-shield blockage of the partial moments. They are kept in the 1-min file, with `sun_dist_au`, but masked in the hourly file.
  - Encounter 26 perihelion is 2025-12-13T07 UT at 0.0459 AU. Partial-moment densities may still be biased low.
- MAVEN:
  - KP-4SEC is used instead of ONBOARDSVYMOM because KP carries MSO positions.
  - Upstream samples must satisfy all of the following:
    - position outside 1.2x the Vignes et al. (2000) bow shock (X0 = 0.64 RM, ε = 1.03, L = 2.04 RM, RM = 3389.5 km);
    - SWIA density DQ = 1;
    - |v| > 200 km/s and -Vx(MSO) > 0;
    - T < 1e6 K.
  - Beyond 1.2x the median B levels off at about 3.8 nT. Samples above 1e6 K show upstream-like B and are treated as onboard-moment artifacts.
  - Onboard moments assume 100% protons, so T is biased high (median about 2e5 K).
  - A density excursion to 50–125 cm^-3 on 2025-10-29, with B about 11 nT, is retained as possibly real.
  - Mars solar conjunction is in January 2026, and CDAWeb data stop on 2025-12-05.
- BepiColombo is 21 deg and Mercury 7 deg in HGI longitude from the comet at about 0.35 AU, but no BepiColombo cruise plasma or field data are on CDAWeb.
- HAPI sometimes returns a record outside the requested interval, for example at the edge of a gap. Each chunk is clipped to its own [start, end) range.
